info.desc: White Blood Cells is the third album by American garage rock band The White Stripes, released in 2001. Considered the band's commercial breakthrough, White Blood Cells peaked at number 61 on the Billboard 200, going Gold and selling over 500,000 units. The album also reached number 55 in the United Kingdom, being bolstered in both territories by the Fell in Love with a Girl single and its Lego-animation music video. Stylus magazine rated it the fifteenth greatest album of 2000-2005 while Pitchfork Media ranked it ninth on their list of the top 100 albums from 2000-2004. The album was dedicated .

podcast.body: This album achieved substantial success, selling a million copies in the US and another million globally for Sympathy for the Record Industry. It tapped into a public desire for stripped-down, authentic rock and was confidently recommended by a record store clerk as a band "everybody will be talking about." "The third white stripes album for the label sold a million copies in the US and another million globally. I walked into the store, asked for what all the cool kids were buying and the guy behind the counter handed me a copy of white blood cells. Here you go, mate, he says, soon everybody will be talking about this band from Detroit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album became a widespread phenomenon, far exceeding all expectations upon its release. Its initial indie label, Sympathy for the Record Industry, was unable to meet the overwhelming demand, leading to its re-release in 2002 by UB2 Records, which had a greater reach and helped propel the album to international markets and boost the band's fame. "White Blood Sales se lanzó en 2001 y se oconverteó en un fenómeno, superando todas las expectativas."

srcs.episode: Por qué White Stripes desaparecieron en su mejor momento?

podcast.body: This album was released by The White Stripes just three weeks before The Strokes' debut album came out in July 2001. This timing placed both bands at the forefront of the burgeoning Garage Rock revival, contributing to its critical mass. "The White Stripes from their White Blood sales album released just three weeks before the Strokes came out with their debut album, so good timing in retrospect."
